learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic principles of program creation.
Knows programming techniques in C and C++ languages.
Has the ability to solve problematic professional tasks in the field of computer science.
Is able to use compilation software.
Is aware of the responsibility for their own work and readiness to adhere to teamwork principles and take responsibility for jointly implemented tasks.

syllabus_topics: Lectures: Programming in C++: program structure, compilation, preprocessor directives, variables; pointers and references, namespaces; execution control: conditional statements, loops, recursion; functions; complex data structures: arrays, structures, classes; dynamic memory allocation. Basics of object-oriented programming: classes: members and methods; constructors; destructors; operator overloading; inheritance and polymorphism; exceptions; casting.

Laboratory exercises: Laboratory exercises are conducted as part of the subject. The content of these classes consolidates and expands the knowledge conveyed during lectures. They allow applying knowledge in practice. Students, under the guidance of the instructor and using prepared instructions, create their own programs. They learn to devise and implement simple algorithms.
assessment_rules: The condition for passing the laboratory classes is to obtain at least half of the points from the developed programs, exercises performed during laboratories, and any tests. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
